items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And did you know Frank Mutz, piano player? The name doesn't ring any bells, no.

ctx.x: Something we could look up somehow. I might be able to find him in the dead files downstairs. Dead in the sense that we don't use him anymore. I don't know how he got the nickname, but that was a distinguishing from Santo to Trombone player. Sure, yeah. And when did you meet him? Oh somewhere, I would say about midway in my career, because he was Santo's younger. And he played a few jobs with us, with the dance band part of the Donbusters. We were playing night jobs, parties of clubs and things like that. And the…
Pec. Yeah. And did you know Frank Mutz, piano player? The name doesn't ring any bells, no. When did you join the union?

I became a member, let me think now, I guess it would have been about 19, about 27. I'd have to look that up myself. The union at that time was on Royal Street in the 300 block, roughly about 305, something like that, on the second or third floor. And I heard about a drive they were having for new members in which the initiation fee was lowered to $15. And so a whole raft of us went in, because in those days, you weren't considered a professional musician unless you were in the union. Because all the guys who…
